summary: Iter 55 — Super Marketplace Phase A1 (Shop foundation) backend-only testing. 34/34 pytest passed in test_iter55_marketplace_phase_a.py covering: (a) Consumer public /api/shop/{categories,home,businesses,businesses/{id}} — 9 seeded categories present (restaurant/retail/beauty/home_services/professional/fitness/automotive/events/other), shop_home returns headline='SHOP LOCAL. EARN BIGPOINTS.' + 5 sections (recommended/earn_more/food/services/featured), /businesses only returns status=approved profiles (verified against Mongo), unknown business detail → 404. (b) Auth guards: merchant endpoints → 401 without token; admin endpoints → 401 without token and → 403 for demo listener (correct role gating). (c) Merchant /api/merchant/marketplace/onboarding validations ALL fire correctly with proper error codes: bad_category, commission_agreement_required, bigpoints_required, below_min_bigpoints, price_parity_required (restaurant). Happy-path onboarding creates a pending marketplace_profile + mirrors into businesses (inactive) + creates merchant_bigpoint_accounts row. /profile, /bigpoints/settings GET+PATCH (with below_min guard), /bigpoints/preview by both `points` AND `order_value_cents` (100 pts = $3.00; $50 order @ 2 pts/$ = 100 pts = $3.00), /bigpoints/account, /bigpoints/fund (Stripe checkout_url + session_id, amount = 10000pts * 3.0 = $300), /bigpoints/auto-reload PATCH all work and persist. (d) Admin: GET/POST/PATCH /bigpoint-rates, /categories (dup key → 400), /commission-rules; GET /businesses?status=pending; POST /businesses/{id}/approve (flips profile.status=approved AND businesses.active=verified=true, then business appears in public /api/shop/businesses + /api/shop/businesses/{id} 200); reject unknown → 404; /dashboard returns example_point_cost_cents=3.0 + example_commission for restaurant=15.0. (e) Economics resolver priority verified end-to-end: seeded market(2.5)+category(2.0)+merchant(1.5) rates, then observed preview cost drop from 1.5 → 2.0 → 2.5 → 3.0 (default) as each higher-priority rate is deactivated — confirms merchant > category > market > global specificity.
action_items: None functional — all Phase A1 backend requirements validated.

OPTIONAL (defence-in-depth): /api/merchant/marketplace/onboarding does not check the caller's user role. Any authenticated user (listener, premium, admin) can become a merchant just by POSTing to /onboarding. Consider gating this on an opt-in flag or requiring a distinct 'merchant' role/entitlement after signup, otherwise every listener automatically has a marketplace profile mirror in Mongo. Not blocking for A1 but worth flagging before Phase B (product listings) opens up.

OPTIONAL: /api/merchant/marketplace/bigpoints/preview accepts negative `points` (Pydantic PreviewBody.points has no ge=0). A negative preview will return a negative estimated_cost — cosmetic-only since it's a preview, but tighten with `ge=0`.

OPTIONAL: /api/admin/marketplace/bigpoint-rates POST has no dedupe — inserting many rows with the same (scope,category) is allowed and the resolver relies on effective_date ordering to pick the newest. Fine for now, but consider a unique-active constraint per scope tuple to prevent silent config drift.

OPTIONAL: /api/admin/marketplace/businesses/{id}/approve returns {ok, status} but does NOT return the updated profile — admin UI has to re-fetch. Cheap improvement to return the profile in the response for one-round-trip UX.
critical_code_review_comments: services/marketplace.py:158 resolve_point_cost_cents — if there are multiple ACTIVE rates in the same scope (e.g., two category=restaurant rates), the resolver picks by max(effective_date). Effective_date is stamped at insert time and cannot be edited via PATCH (only cost/scope/etc are updated) — so the LATEST-INSERTED rate wins, not the latest 'effective_date' the admin might intend. Consider allowing effective_date in RateBody (currently absent), or documenting this behaviour in the admin UI.

routes/marketplace_merchant.py:61 onboarding — commission_agreed and price_parity_certified are stored as plain booleans + timestamp, but there is no immutable audit record (no signed IP/user-agent snapshot, no version of the ToS). For a real marketplace launch these agreements are legally significant; consider persisting a versioned agreement snapshot into a separate collection.

routes/marketplace_merchant.py:81 onboarding — `market` is derived from locations[0].city OR user.market. If neither is present the profile is created with market=None, which then makes market-scoped rates/commissions inapplicable to that merchant. Should either require market or default to a platform default.

routes/marketplace_admin.py:171-175 approve — sets businesses.active/verified=True but does NOT touch marketplace_profiles.commission_rule_id or point_cost snapshot. If admin later changes the category commission_pct, existing 'approved' businesses inherit the new rate silently. Fine for A1 but flag for order-time economics snapshotting in Phase B.

routes/marketplace_merchant.py:213 bp_fund — inserts a bigpoint_funding_transactions row with status=pending BEFORE returning the checkout_url, but Stripe session creation happens INSIDE the same request. If Stripe returns success but the DB insert fails (network/mongo hiccup), the merchant would see the checkout URL but never have a pending txn — status polling later would 404. Wrap stripe.create + db.insert in a try/except and if the insert fails, cancel the Stripe session (or at minimum log for reconciliation).

routes/marketplace_merchant.py:243 bp_fund_status — a stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve failure is silently swallowed and the endpoint returns status=pending, which may hide a real payment (paid on Stripe but DB never credited). Should log the exception and expose a 503 or a distinct 'unknown' status so admin can reconcile.

routes/shop.py:60 businesses — server-side sort=featured re-sorts a limited page (max 100) client-side. If there are >100 approved businesses, featured/sponsored ones past the cutoff will be invisible in the featured sort. Push sort into the MongoDB query (secondary index on {status:1, sponsored:-1, featured:-1}).

routes/shop.py:94 shop_home — makes 5 separate collection scans per request (recommended/most_points/food/services/featured). At scale, batch via a single aggregation with $facet, and add a small in-memory TTL cache — this endpoint is likely the hottest read path in the shop.

services/marketplace.py:29 seed_marketplace_foundation — commission_pct is duplicated between marketplace_categories (denormalized) and marketplace_commission_rules (source of truth). The consumer/merchant code sometimes reads cat.commission_pct directly (never through the resolver) which can drift once admin edits a rule but not the category doc. Recommend removing commission_pct from the category doc entirely and always going through resolve_commission().

routes/marketplace_admin.py: none of the admin write endpoints (create_rate/create_category/create_commission/approve/reject) write to an admin_audit_log. For any regulated marketplace this is a compliance requirement — should log actor_user_id + before/after diff on every mutation.
test_credentials: Demo listener: POST /api/auth/demo -> use session_token as Bearer (demo@bigfm.dubai). Admin: no email/password route — the test file directly inserts a row into `sessions` for user with email=admin@bigfm.dubai (user_id resolved from mongo) with a random `sess_iter55_<hex>` token and expires_at=now+2h; the token is cleaned up in fixture teardown.
seed_data_creation: Test uses ephemeral seeds: (1) demo user's marketplace_profile becomes 'approved' at end of TestApprovalFlow — this state persists after the run (needed for repeated re-runs, and the onboarding test re-upserts the same business_id). (2) TestEconomicsResolvers creates 3 bigpoint_rates rows (market/category/merchant scope) and DELETES them in a try/finally. (3) TestAdminCRUD creates + DELETES one rate, one category (key=TEST_cat_iter55), one commission rule. (4) admin_token fixture inserts + deletes one sessions row. No orphan test data left behind except the promoted demo business (intentional, and idempotent under re-run).
context_for_next_testing_agent: REGRESSION FILE: /app/backend/tests/test_iter55_marketplace_phase_a.py — 34 pytest tests covering Phase A1 (shop/merchant/admin marketplace). To re-run: `cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> python -m pytest tests/test_iter55_marketplace_phase_a.py -v`. GOTCHA: `requests.Session` naturally persists Set-Cookie from POST /api/auth/demo — this leaks demo auth into subsequent admin Bearer calls because auth.py:_resolve_user_from_request checks cookies FIRST then Bearer. The test file uses a _NoCookieSession subclass that clears cookies after every request; future marketplace tests should do the same OR use separate `requests.Session()` per user role. Admin auth pattern: no login route exists — insert a `sessions` doc {user_id: <admin user_id>, token: 'sess_...', expires_at: future} then send as Bearer. TestApprovalFlow leaves demo's marketplace_profile in status=approved; if you want a fresh 'pending' repro, delete profile+business rows for demo before re-run OR run only TestMerchantOnboardingValidations (that test path is idempotent since /onboarding upserts on owner_user_id).
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs found in the marketplace backend. One test infra issue (cookie leak between demo and admin bearer calls in the shared requests.Session) was fixed inside the test file via a _NoCookieSession subclass. All happy paths, all documented validation error codes, all auth guards, and the merchant>category>market>global resolver specificity are verified end-to-end against the running backend + Mongo state.
